results.content: Ghanaian Afrobeats and Highlife singer-songwriter King Promise says his ambition is to take Ghanaian music to the global stage without losing the sound and identity that distinguish local artistes from their international counterparts.

results.title: I compete with myself, not other artistes – King Promise
results.content: Ghanaian Afrobeats and Highlife singer-songwriter Gregory Bortey Newman, known popularly as King Promise, says he is more focused on improving his own achievements than competing with fellow artistes, describing his approach to the music industry as a continuous pursuit of personal growth.

results.title: UBA Foundation opens 2026 essay competition to promote literacy among SHS students
results.content: The UBA Foundation has opened applications for its 2026 National Essay Competition, seeking to strengthen the writing skills, creativity and critical thinking of senior high school students across Ghana amid concerns about declining literacy skills among young people. The competition offers students an opportunity to develop their writing abilities, express their ideas and compete for financial support towards their tertiary education. Regional Head of Brand, Marketing and Corporate Communications at UBA West Africa, Henry Nii Dottey, said the initiative formed part of the foundation’s efforts to support education and nurture the creative potential of young people.

results.title: GRASAG president calls for sustainable funding for agricultural research in Africa
results.content: The President of the Graduate Students Association of Ghana (GRASAG), Richard Class-Peters, has called for sustainable financing for agricultural research to improve food security, boost local production and support economic growth across Africa. He made the call at the recently concluded World Bank’s Africa Growth and Opportunity – Research in Action (AGORA) 2026 conference in Palermo, Italy. Mr Class-Peters said African countries must increase investment in research and innovation while strengthening farmer cooperatives to improve agricultural productivity and build more resilient food systems. “Sustainable financing for agricultural research is critical to empowering innovation, strengthening farmer cooperatives and transforming local agriculture for food security and economic prosperity in Africa,” he said.

results.title: Ghana to review laws to implement Accra Convention – Ofosu-Adjare
results.content: The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, says Ghana will review its laws to facilitate the implementation of the Accra Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents, a move expected to improve businesses' access to trade financing. Speaking at the signing ceremony in Accra, she said the Convention would address inequalities in access to credit, particularly for businesses transporting goods by road that often struggle to use cargo as collateral for loans. “There are fewer ways to raise finance for one whose goods are on a truck than one whose goods are on a ship. That is the imbalance this Convention was written to correct,” she said.

results.title: Ghana’s ambassador to Côte d’Ivoire extends consular outreach to four western towns
results.content: Ghana's Ambassador to Côte d'Ivoire, Brigadier General Alhassan Abu (rtd), has extended the Embassy's diaspora engagement and consular outreach programme to Ghanaians living in San Pedro, Sassandra, Grand Lahou and Tabou in western Côte d'Ivoire. The initiative is aimed at strengthening ties with Ghanaians living outside Abidjan, improving access to consular services and addressing concerns affecting their welfare and protection. During engagements with the Ghanaian communities, the Ambassador conveyed the greetings of President John Dramani Mahama and the government, assuring them of the Embassy's commitment to protecting their interests in the host country. He explained that the Ghana Embassy in Abidjan was responsible for maintaining diplomatic relations between Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire, as well as promoting Ghana's national interests and protecting its citizens. results.title: Fameye to light up ‘December in Juaben’ homecoming festival
results.content: Ghanaian musician Fameye is set to bring his music to Juaben this December as the annual “December in Juaben” homecoming festival returns with four days of entertainment, culture and community activities. Organised by the Richmond Amoateng Foundation, the festival will run from December 24 to 27, 2026, bringing residents, returning natives and visitors together under the theme, “Reconnecting Roots, Celebrating Heritage & Building Juabenman Together.” Fameye will perform alongside other artistes at the carnival night on December 26, with Adu Boaheng Park advertised as the venue. Seleka Shaker will be on DJ duties, while Highest MC will serve as hypeman.

results.title: Government must take decisive and far-reaching action on Obuasi SHTS case – Methodist Church Ghana
results.content: The Methodist Church Ghana has called on the government to take decisive and far-reaching action on allegations of sexual abuse involving 19 female students of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS). The Church is demanding an independent and transparent investigation into the allegations against the school's headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, as well as accountability for any officials or institutions whose actions or inaction may have contributed to the alleged abuse. The allegations involving Obuasi SHTS have attracted national attention, with the number of students reportedly alleging abuse reaching 19.

results.title: MoMo Fest 2026 promotes cashless shopping and digital financial inclusion in Kumasi
results.content: MoMo Fest 2026 has brought digital payments to traders and consumers at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi, allowing festival-goers to purchase food, clothing and other goods using mobile money. The event, supported by Mobile Money Fintech Ltd (MMFL), combined live entertainment with a marketplace featuring local vendors, with the MoMo App serving as the primary platform for transactions. Organisers say the initiative is aimed at expanding digital financial inclusion, encouraging businesses to adopt cashless payment systems and educating users on safer mobile money transactions. MTN Kumasi Territory Sales Controller, Samuel Owusu Baah, said the festival was designed to extend financial services to people at the grassroots level by making digital payments more accessible to traders and consumers.

results.title: Three arrested in Atewa Forest as NAIMOS launches Operation Green Shield
results.content: Three people have been arrested in the Atewa Forest Reserve in the Eastern Region as the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) launches a military-backed operation to flush out illegal miners and protect the threatened forest. The arrests were made on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, as part of Operation Green Shield, an initiative designed to disrupt illegal mining, clear affected areas and maintain a security presence to prevent miners from returning. The Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, described the destruction of Ghana's forest reserves through illegal mining as a national emergency, warning that the activities were threatening the country's environment, water resources and future generations.

results.title: IERPP demands account of $4bn 24-Hour Economy before rollout of $10bn New Economy
results.content: The Institute of Economic Research and Public Policy (IERPP) has challenged the Mahama administration to account for the financing, projects and jobs associated with its $4 billion 24-Hour Economy programme before proceeding with the proposed $10 billion New Economy initiative. The institute’s Executive Director, Professor Isaac Boadi, says the government must provide verifiable evidence of the original programme’s performance, including funds disbursed, projects implemented and employment created. Speaking at a press conference at the IERPP Conference Room in Adabraka, Accra, on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, he questioned the credibility of announcing a substantially larger economic initiative without first publishing a comprehensive account of the existing programme.

results.title: African climate lead demands action for local communities at Liberia summit
results.content: At a strategic gathering of climate negotiators and national focal points, the African Group of Negotiators (AGN) issued a direct call to prioritize local implementation over international diplomacy alone, warning that global agreements mean little if they do not empower everyday citizens.

results.title: Adu-Boahene trial must be decided on evidence, not public pressure – Group
results.content: A group has called for the protection of the judge presiding over the criminal trial of former National Signals Bureau director Kwabena Adu-Boahene and two others from political pressure and other forms of improper influence. The group, convened by Rev. DK Odei-Appiah, said Justice Francis Apangabuno Achibonga must be allowed to determine the case independently, without intimidation or public pressure to deliver a particular outcome. Speaking at a press conference at the Ghana International Press Centre in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, Rev. Odei-Appiah said the coalition’s intervention was intended to protect judicial independence, the presumption of innocence and public confidence in Ghana’s criminal justice system.
